L17@P0: If approved, this resolution will result in an expenditure contract with Insight Housing

L42@P1: assisted indoors or into places of greater safety. By developing a resource specifically
L43@P1: tailored to the needs of the encampment, the City can assist everyone that wants a shelter
L44@P1: bed to get indoors and work with remaining residents to identify a safer alternative.
L45@P1: Further, we have not yet had a dedicated funding source to appropriately serve these
L46@P1: encampments in their entirety (which together have an estimated 40 residents); by finding
L47@P1: a resolution to this geographic area, we can more equitably redistribute resources to other
L48@P1: areas of the city that require assistance.

L94@P2: Helping unhoused people currently living in West Berkeley transition into interim and
L95@P2: permanent housing placement will minimize the detrimental environmental impacts
L96@P2: associated with encampment homelessness over the long run, including vector and fire
L97@P2: hazards, accumulation of trash and waste, and impacts on sensitive waterways. It will
L98@P2: also reduce negative impacts of environmental elements on the health and safety of those
L99@P2: living in these encampments.
L100@P2: RATIONALE FOR RECOMMENDATION
L101@P2: Insight Housing will be the main social service provider for the proposal and has been
L102@P2: providing services in our community since 1970, including: emergency food and shelter,
L103@P2: transitional housing, rapid rehousing, and permanent supportive housing with support
L104@P2: services to individuals and families. Insight Housing also has experience operating noncongregate shelter in Berkeley, having operated a Project Roomkey site during the
L105@P2: pandemic.
